FT-IR Analysis\n[原文]\n$\\triangle \\nu = \\nu _ { 0 } - \\nu , \\nu _ { 0 }$ is the monomeric OH stretching frequency, which is taken to be $3 6 0 0 { \\mathrm { c m } } ^ { - 1 }$ , ν is the stretching frequency $( \\mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 } )$ observed in the infrared spectrum of the sample, and R is the H-bonding distance (Å).\n\nThe spectral was normalized $\\mathsf { a t 1 0 1 6 ~ c m ^ { - 1 } }$ and the derivative curve was obtained by applying the Savitzky–Golay algorithm. The wavenumbers of H-bonding components are taken from second-derivative spectra according to regions that are assigned to various H-bonds. Nonlinear fitting of the FT-IR spectral region from $\\bar { 3 } 0 0 0 \\mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 }$ to $3 7 0 0 ~ \\mathrm { c m } ^ { - \\mathrm { 1 } }$ was carried out with Gaussian function in Peakfit 4.12 software (SeaSolve Software Inc., Framingham, MA, USA). The Pearson correlation coeficients were evaluated between the CI and content of various H-bonds, with a statistically significant p-value of <0.05, while using Spss 25.0 statistics software (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA).\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.1. The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\n[原文]\nFor softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, the macro-fibrillation index and the fiber length had a downward trend, and the fines content has an upward trend for the softwood fibers during PFI refining, as can be seen in Figure 1. The macro-fibrillation index and fiber length of softwood fibers changed significantly. However, two parameters of hardwood fibers had no significant variations relative to softwood fibers. It might be because of the lower refining pressure that was applied in hardwood fibers. The macro-fibrillation index characterizes external macro-fibrillation. The results of fiber morphology analysis showed that external fibrillation increased with the refining process. It is consistent with the increasing specific surface area (as shown in Table S1 in Online Resource).",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the differences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H···O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds differed at various refining stages.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.",

解析修复95块 · 要点 2/3；边界 1/2

FT-IR谱先以1016 cm−1进行归一化，并用Savitzky–Golay算法获得导数曲线。 [2]
不同氢键组分的波数取自二阶导数谱中对应各氢键归属区域的峰位。 [2]
对3000–3700 cm−1的FT-IR谱段采用Gaussian函数进行非线性拟合，软件为Peakfit 4.12。 [2]
羟基谱带（3000–3700 cm−1）被解卷积为四个主要谱带。 [4]
各氢键的相对含量按相应谱带的面积比例计算。 [4]
峰位归属包括约3227 cm−1的O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键、约3346 cm−1的O(3)H···O(5)分子内氢键和约3452 cm−1的O(2)H···O(6)分子内氢键。 [4]

      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the differences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H···O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds differed at various refining stages.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.",

PyMuPDF结构81块 · 要点 2/3；边界 1/2

论文将3000–3700 cm−1的羟基吸收带解卷积为四个主要子峰，并依据各子峰的面积占比分别计算不同氢键的相对含量。 [2] [3]
拟合前光谱在1016 cm−1归一化，并用Savitzky–Golay算法获得导数曲线；各氢键组分的峰位取自二阶导数谱，并按不同氢键归属区确定。 [3]
对3000–3700 cm−1区间采用Gaussian函数，在Peakfit 4.12软件中进行非线性拟合。 [3]
各氢键的归属区间为：3580–3550 cm−1对应free OH(2)和OH(6)，3455–3410 cm−1对应O(2)H···O(6)分子内氢键，3375–3340 cm−1对应O(3)H···O(5)分子内氢键，3310–3230 cm−1对应O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键（cellulose I）。 [6]
文中还给出约3227、3346、3452 cm−1分别对应O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键、O(3)H···O(5)分子内氢键和O(2)H···O(6)分子内氢键。 [2]

      "text": "论文将3000–3700 cm−1的羟基吸收带解卷积为四个主要子峰，并依据各子峰的面积占比分别计算不同氢键的相对含量。",
      "citation_refs": [
        "[2]",
        "[3]"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "C2",
      "text": "拟合前光谱在1016 cm−1归一化，并用Savitzky–Golay算法获得导数曲线；各氢键组分的峰位取自二阶导数谱，并按不同氢键归属区确定。",
      "citation_refs": [
        "[3]"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "C3",
      "text": "对3000–3700 cm−1区间采用Gaussian函数，在Peakfit 4.12软件中进行非线性拟合。",
      "citation_refs": [
        "[3]"
      ]
    },

      "text": "各氢键的归属区间为：3580–3550 cm−1对应free OH(2)和OH(6)，3455–3410 cm−1对应O(2)H···O(6)分子内氢键，3375–3340 cm−1对应O(3)H···O(5)分子内氢键，3310–3230 cm−1对应O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键（cellulose I）。",

      "text": "Polymers 2020, 12, 2912 8 of 14\nThe peak position assigned to O(6)H· · · O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds (around 3227 cm−1),\nO(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds (around 3346 cm−1), and O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds\n(around 3452 cm−1) of softwood ﬁbers and hardwood ﬁbers almost kept constant in the whole reﬁning\nprocess, as shown in Figure 6a,b. According to the formulae of H-bonding energy and H-bonding\ndistance (Equations (4) and (5)), the H-bonding energies and H-bonding distances of the three H-bonds\nremained unchanged, as the peak positions of three H-bonds almost did not exhibit red shift or blue\nshift. The results showed that PFI reﬁning did not change the H-bonding energies and H-bonding\ndistances, just as it did not change the cellulose polymorph in the above results.\n\nFigure 6. The second derivative of the Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR) spectra for\nthe reﬁned and unreﬁned samples: (a) softwood ﬁber and (b) hardwood ﬁber.\nBecause the recorded infrared spectrum is the convolution of the real spectrum and the linear\nfunction of instrument. Subsequently, the relative\ncontent of various H-bonds was calculated based on area proportion of the band, respectively.       "text": "Additionally, it was probably due to the weaker cleavage eﬀect on (200) lattice planes that was hard for\nwater molecules to penetrate.\n\n3.3. Eﬀect of PFI Reﬁning on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\nA mixture of inter-molecular and intra-molecular H-bonds is considered to be the cause for the\nbroadening of OH bands in the FT-IR spectra. Therefore, taking derivative of the OH bands can improve\nthe resolution of various H-bonds. XRD Analysis\nThe crystallinity of pretreated ﬁbers was determined by a Shimadzu XRD 7000S (Shimadzu,\nKyoto, Japan), while using Cu-Ka radiation. The samples were scanned at 40 kV and 30 mA in a 2θ\nrange of 4–40◦at 1◦/min. It is well known that two polymorphs, cellulose Iα and Iβ, are present in\nnative cellulose; for clarity, all of the reﬂections indexed here are on the Iβ lattice. Before analysis,\nthe experimental data is nine point smoothed with Savitzky–Golay algorithm. The two types of CI\nvalues were obtained from peak intensity method (CI −XI) and peak ﬁtting (CI-XA), respectively.\nThe CI −XI was calculated as in Equation (2) [19].\n(I200 −Iam) CI −XI = × 100% (2)\nI200\nwhere I200 is the maximum diﬀraction intensity value of the (200) lattice plane between the scattering\nangles of 2θ = 22◦and 23◦, and Iam is the minimum diﬀraction intensity of amorphous fraction between\n2θ = 18◦and 19◦.\nAll of the XRD diﬀractograms were smoothed with the Savitzky–Golay algorithm and\nbaseline-corrected with linear ﬁt function. Subsequently, the baseline-corrected diﬀractograms\nwere deconvoluted with the Pearson VII function. The value of the CI-XA equals the area percentage\noccupied by crystalline peaks over the total area of the diﬀraction pattern [20]. In addition, the crystallite\nsize was calculated by the widely used Scherrer Equation (3) [21]:\nk × λ\nL = (3)\n(β × cos θ)\nwhere L is the size that is perpendicular to the lattice plane, k is a constant that depends on the crystal\nshape (0.89), λ is the wavelength of the incident beam in the diﬀraction experiment (0.154 nm), β is the\nfull width at half maximum of the diﬀraction peak, and θ is the Bragg’s angle. In general, the values of\nthe calculated crystallite sizes might be lower than that of the real crystallite sizes, because the peak\nbroadening from the instrumental factors was not considered [22].\n\n2.5.       "Polymers 2020, 12, 2912 2 of 14\nﬁrst and then decreased with the degree of reﬁning for hardwood bleached kraft pulp ﬁbers [11] or\nfor unbleached eucalyptus ﬁbers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially\nﬂuctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating ﬂuctuation with PFI reﬁning for\ntobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identiﬁed a clear trend, but the results\nwere that the crystallinity varied during PFI reﬁnement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in\ncrystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during\nPFI reﬁning.\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure,\ncan be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl\ngroups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding\ndistance during deligniﬁcation [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used\nto study the diﬀerences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal\nregion [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during\nPFI reﬁning, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of\neucalyptus ﬁbers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that\nthe H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions\nof the content of certain H-bonds diﬀered at various reﬁning stages.\n\nThere is still a lack of literature on the eﬀects of PFI reﬁnement on the H-bonding network.\nParticularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of\nfurther study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of\nH-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, ﬂexibility,\nand ﬁbrillation of cellulosic ﬁbers during PFI reﬁnement. Therefore, this work explored the eﬀects\nof PFI reﬁnement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of\nH-bonds for softwood pulp ﬁbers and hardwood pulp ﬁbers. Attempts were made in order to establish\nthe correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.",
      "Polymers 2020, 12, 2912 9 of 14\n\nFigure 7. The deconvoluted FT-IR spectra of softwood ﬁbers at various revolutions: (a) 0 r, (b) 4000 r,\n(c) 8000 r, (d) 12,000 r, and (e) 16,000 r.\nFor the content of O(6)H· · · O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds of softwood ﬁber, the trend can be\ndivided into two stages, as shown in Table 2a. It decreased by 7.72% from 28.23% to 26.05% as reﬁning\nfrom 0r to 4000 r and then increased by 9.14% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by a decrease of 17.13%,\nwith the revolutions increasing from 8000 r to 16,000 r. Regarding the O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds of\nhardwood ﬁber, the trend was almost similar to that of softwood ﬁbers, except for a small increase of\n0.45% from 8000 r to 12,000 r (in Table 2b). On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds\nfor softwood ﬁbers and hardwood ﬁbers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively.\nThe decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical\naction of PFI reﬁning, which was closely related to internal and external ﬁbrillation (as seen in\nSection 3.1).       "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \\mathrm { H } \\cdots \\mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nIn the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood fiber, the trend of content can be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend in general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the breakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and higher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose more accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups, which makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H···O(6) or O(6)H···O(3′)H-bonds. Thus although there is the formation of free OH(2) and OH(6) during fibrillation, the content of the free OH(2) and OH(6) might disease; meanwhile, the content of the O(6)H···O(3′) or the O(2)H···O(6) H-bonds might increase upon drying.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.4. Correlation between CI and Content of Inter-Molecular H-Bonds during PFI Refining\n[原文]\nSimilar to the CI-XI, the content of O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds decreased first and then had an increase, followed by a decline for the two fibers (as shown in Figure 8a,b). Besides, the Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated between the content of H-bonds and the CI-XI. It was 0.912 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. The similar trends in the content of the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds and the CI-XI might be because that the crystalline region has a higher content of O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds when compared with the amorphous regions, as illustrated in Figure 9 [35].",

Regarding the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, the trend was almost similar to that of softwood fibers, except for a small increase of 0.45% from 8000 r to 12,000 r (in Table 2b). The O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds is stable, as mentioned above. It was presumed to change little as crystallinity changed during PFI refining. During the whole refining, the amount of $\\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \\mathrm { H } \\cdots \\mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nIn the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood fiber, the trend of content can be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend in general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the breakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and higher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose more accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups, which makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H···O(6) or O(6)H···O(3′)H-bonds. Thus although there is the formation of free OH(2) and OH(6) during fibrillation, the content of the free OH(2) and OH(6) might disease; meanwhile, the content of the O(6)H···O(3′) or the O(2)H···O(6) H-bonds might increase upon drying.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.4. Correlation between CI and Content of Inter-Molecular H-Bonds during PFI Refining\n[原文]\nSimilar to the CI-XI, the content of O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds decreased first and then had an increase, followed by a decline for the two fibers (as shown in Figure 8a,b). Besides, the Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated between the content of H-bonds and the CI-XI. It was 0.912 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. The similar trends in the content of the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds and the CI-XI might be because that the crystalline region has a higher content of O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds when compared with the amorphous regions, as illustrated in Figure 9 [35].",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nThe peak position assigned to $\\mathrm { O } ( 6 ) \\mathrm { H } \\cdots \\mathrm { O } ( 3 ^ { \\prime } )$ inter-molecular H-bonds (around $3 2 2 7 ~ \\mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 } )$ O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds (around 3346 cm<sup>−1</sup>), and O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds (around 3452 cm<sup>−1</sup>) of softwood fibers and hardwood fibers almost kept constant in the whole refining process, as shown in Figure 6a,b. According to the formulae of H-bonding energy and H-bonding distance (Equations (4) and (5)), the H-bonding energies and H-bonding distances of the three H-bonds remained unchanged, as the peak positions of three H-bonds almost did not exhibit red shift or blue shift. The results showed that PFI refining did not change the H-bonding energies and H-bonding distances, just as it did not change the cellulose polymorph in the above results\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. It decreased by 7.72% from 28.23% to 26.05% as refining from 0r to 4000 r and then increased by 9.14% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by a decrease of 17.13%, with the revolutions increasing from 8000 r to 16,000 r. Regarding the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, the trend was almost similar to that of softwood fibers, except for a small increase of 0.45% from 8000 r to 12,000 r (in Table 2b). On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Correlation between CI and Content of Inter-Molecular H-Bonds during PFI Refining\n[原文]\nThe correlation between the CI-XI and the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds or the free OH(2) and OH(6) was poor for the following reasons. The free OH groups are easier for forming the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds as opposed to the O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds in the amorphous region, because the distance between adjacent glucose units in a cellulosic molecular chain is closer than between the glucose units in the adjacent molecular chain (as shown in Figure 9). Accordingly, when compared with the content of O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds, there was less difference in the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds or the free OH groups between the crystalline region and amorphous region, which sometimes made the content of the two bonds not change much in regards to the crystallinity. The O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds is stable, as mentioned above. It was presumed to change little as crystallinity changed during PFI refining. Hence, the correlation between O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds and the CI-XI was not discussed in the present study.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. It is well known that two polymorphs, cellulose Iα and Iβ, are present in\nnative cellulose; for clarity, all of the reﬂections indexed here are on the Iβ lattice. Before analysis,\nthe experimental data is nine point smoothed with Savitzky–Golay algorithm. The two types of CI\nvalues were obtained from peak intensity method (CI −XI) and peak ﬁtting (CI-XA), respectively.\nThe CI −XI was calculated as in Equation (2) [19].\n(I200 −Iam) CI −XI = × 100% (2)\nI200\nwhere I200 is the maximum diﬀraction intensity value of the (200) lattice plane between the scattering\nangles of 2θ = 22◦and 23◦, and Iam is the minimum diﬀraction intensity of amorphous fraction between\n2θ = 18◦and 19◦.\nAll of the XRD diﬀractograms were smoothed with the Savitzky–Golay algorithm and\nbaseline-corrected with linear ﬁt function. Subsequently, the baseline-corrected diﬀractograms\nwere deconvoluted with the Pearson VII function. The value of the CI-XA equals the area percentage\noccupied by crystalline peaks over the total area of the diﬀraction pattern [20]. In addition, the crystallite\nsize was calculated by the widely used Scherrer Equation (3) [21]:\nk × λ\nL = (3)\n(β × cos θ)\nwhere L is the size that is perpendicular to the lattice plane, k is a constant that depends on the crystal\nshape (0.89), λ is the wavelength of the incident beam in the diﬀraction experiment (0.154 nm), β is the\nfull width at half maximum of the diﬀraction peak, and θ is the Bragg’s angle. In general, the values of\nthe calculated crystallite sizes might be lower than that of the real crystallite sizes, because the peak\nbroadening from the instrumental factors was not considered [22].\n\n2.5.       "Figure 8. The trend of the CI-XI, the CI-XA, and the O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds: (a) softwood ﬁbers and\n(b) hardwood ﬁbers.\n\nFigure 9. The illustration of a two-phase structure of cellulose.\nThe correlation between the CI-XI and the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds or the free OH(2) and OH(6)\nwas poor for the following reasons. The free OH groups are easier for forming the O(2)H· · · O(6)\nH-bonds as opposed to the O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds in the amorphous region, because the distance\nbetween adjacent glucose units in a cellulosic molecular chain is closer than between the glucose units\nin the adjacent molecular chain (as shown in Figure 9). Accordingly, when compared with the content\nof O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds, there was less diﬀerence in the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds or the\nfree OH groups between the crystalline region and amorphous region, which sometimes made the\ncontent of the two bonds not change much in regards to the crystallinity. The O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds\nis stable, as mentioned above. It was presumed to change little as crystallinity changed during PFI\nreﬁning. Hence, the correlation between O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds and the CI-XI was not discussed in the\npresent study.\n\n4. Conclusions\nPFI reﬁning acts not only on the macro-level structure and mechanical properties, but also on\nthe supramolecular structure, including crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds.",
      "Polymers 2020, 12, 2912 10 of 14\nthe formation of O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI\n(as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the ﬂexibility of cellulosic ﬁbers, due to the higher mobility\nof molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of ﬁbers (as seen in Section 3.1).\nAs to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood ﬁber, the content had a growth\nof 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of reﬁning from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight\ndecrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of reﬁning.\nOverall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood ﬁbers, which ﬁrst increased and then had a\ndecrease, followed by a growth. During the whole reﬁning, the amount of O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds for\nsoftwood ﬁbers and hardwood ﬁbers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%,\nrespectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only\nless breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the\namorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important\nrole in the cellulose stiﬀness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose\nstiﬀness [33,34].\n\nIn the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood ﬁber, the trend of content\ncan be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of reﬁning\nfrom 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26%\nin the last reﬁning stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood ﬁber, it increased\nﬁrstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both ﬁbers, the content of\nO(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of reﬁning from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to\nthe fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than\nO(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.\nAs to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend\nin general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the\nbreakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and\nhigher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose\nmore accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber,\nthe number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions\nincreasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to\n12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups,\nwhich makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H···O(6) or O(6)H···O(3′)H-bonds. Thus although\nthere is the formation of free OH(2) and OH(6) during fibrillation, the content of the free OH(2) and OH(6)\nmight disease; meanwhile, the content of the O(6)H···O(3′) or the O(2)H···O(6) H-bonds might increase\nupon drying.\n\n3.4. Correlation between CI and Content of Inter-Molecular H-Bonds during PFI Reﬁning\nSimilar to the CI-XI, the content of O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds decreased ﬁrst and then had an increase,\nfollowed by a decline for the two ﬁbers (as shown in Figure 8a,b). Besides, the Pearson correlation\ncoeﬃcients were calculated between the content of H-bonds and the CI-XI. It was 0.912 (p < 0.05)\nfor softwood ﬁbers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood ﬁbers, respectively. The similar trends in the\ncontent of the O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds and the CI-XI might be because that the crystalline region has a\nhigher content of O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds when compared with the amorphous regions, as illustrated\nin Figure 9 [35].",

PFI2-020 · 论文说打浆后氢键能量和距离基本不变，那是不是说明打浆对氢键网络基本没影响？

参考答案与评分要点

不表示完全不变。本文三类氢键的峰位几乎不变，因此据公式推得能量和距离基本不变；但相对含量仍变化：0到16000转，针叶木分子间氢键由28.23%变为23.56%，阔叶木由26.55%变为24.98%。应区分单类氢键能量/距离与不同组分的相对分布。

表格行检索＋关联补全 · 要点 3/3；边界 2/2

论文发现三种氢键的峰位在整个打浆过程中几乎不变，未出现明显红移或蓝移，因此计算得到的氢键能和氢键距离基本不变。 [1]
同一研究指出，打浆后纤维素多晶型、氢键距离和氢键能几乎不变，但结晶指数、微晶尺寸以及各类氢键的含量会随打浆发生变化。 [4]
表中三种氢键的相对含量随打浆转数变化，例如软木纤维的 O(6)H···O(3′) 氢键含量并非恒定，而是在不同打浆阶段升降。 [6]
研究还指出 O(6)H···O(3′) 氢键在打浆过程中既有断裂也有形成，软木和硬木纤维总体上分别下降约 16.54% 和 5.91%。 [9]
因此，打浆对氢键网络的影响不能仅凭氢键能和距离不变来判断；更合理的结论是氢键的固有强度/距离基本不变，但氢键网络的数量、比例或分布发生了改变。 [1] [4] [9]

      "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nKunpeng Li, Lihong Zhao \\* and Beihai He\n\nState Key Laboratory of Pulp and Paper Engineering, South China University of Technology, 381 Wushan Rd., Tianhe District, Guangzhou 510640, China; felikp@mail.scut.edu.cn (K.L.); ppebhhe@scut.edu.cn (B.H.) \\* Correspondence: zhaolh@scut.edu.cn\n\nReceived: 17 November 2020; Accepted: 2 December 2020; Published: 4 December 2020\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nAbstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that affects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks.       "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the differences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H···O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds differed at various refining stages.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining\n[原文]\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.",

The band of hydroxyl groups $( 3 0 0 0 { - } 3 7 0 0 \\mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 } )$ was deconvoluted into four predominant bands in the present study based on the peak positions above. Subsequently, the relative content of various H-bonds was calculated based on area proportion of the band, respectively. Finally, the data and curves obtained using nonlinear fitting for softwood fibers is shown in Table 2a and Figure 7, and the results of hardwood fibers can be seen in Table 2b and Figure S3.",

Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nFor the content of O(6)H···O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the trend can be divided into two stages, as shown in Table 2a. It decreased by 7.72% from 28.23% to 26.05% as refining from 0r to 4000 r and then increased by 9.14% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by a decrease of 17.13%, with the revolutions increasing from 8000 r to 16,000 r. Regarding the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, the trend was almost similar to that of softwood fibers, except for a small increase of 0.45% from 8000 r to 12,000 r (in Table 2b). On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). 解析修复95块 · 要点 3/3；边界 2/2

论文报告PFI打浆过程中三种氢键的峰位几乎不变，因此由公式计算的氢键能量和氢键距离基本不变。 [1]
但论文摘要同时指出，晶型、氢键距离和氢键能量几乎不变，而结晶指数、晶粒尺寸和各类氢键含量随打浆发生变化。 [4]
表2显示，O(6)H···O(3′)、O(3)H···O(5)、O(2)H···O(6)及自由OH的相对含量在打浆不同转数下发生变化。 [6]
论文结论强调，可及性、润胀和纤丝化的变化与超分子结构密切相关，分子间氢键在纤维素晶体堆叠中起重要作用。 [4]
因此更准确的说法是：打浆主要改变氢键含量/分布及超分子聚集，而不是明显改变单个氢键的能量和距离。 [1] [4] [6]

  "task_id": "PFI2-020",
  "answer": "论文报告PFI打浆过程中三种氢键的峰位几乎不变，因此由公式计算的氢键能量和氢键距离基本不变。 [1]\n但论文摘要同时指出，晶型、氢键距离和氢键能量几乎不变，而结晶指数、晶粒尺寸和各类氢键含量随打浆发生变化。 [4]\n表2显示，O(6)H···O(3′)、O(3)H···O(5)、O(2)H···O(6)及自由OH的相对含量在打浆不同转数下发生变化。 [6]\n论文结论强调，可及性、润胀和纤丝化的变化与超分子结构密切相关，分子间氢键在纤维素晶体堆叠中起重要作用。 [4]\n因此更准确的说法是：打浆主要改变氢键含量/分布及超分子聚集，而不是明显改变单个氢键的能量和距离。 [1] [4] [6]",

      "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nKunpeng Li, Lihong Zhao \\* and Beihai He\n\nState Key Laboratory of Pulp and Paper Engineering, South China University of Technology, 381 Wushan Rd., Tianhe District, Guangzhou 510640, China; felikp@mail.scut.edu.cn (K.L.); ppebhhe@scut.edu.cn (B.H.) \\* Correspondence: zhaolh@scut.edu.cn\n\nReceived: 17 November 2020; Accepted: 2 December 2020; Published: 4 December 2020\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nAbstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that affects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coefficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nKeywords: natural cellulosic fibers; mechanical refining; Crystallinity; Crystallite size; Hydrogen bonds",

Methods > 2.5. FT-IR Analysis\n[原文]\nTHE FT-IR spectra were recorded on solid samples in KBr pellets by means of an FT-IR Bruker Vertex 70 spectrometer (Karlsruhe, Germany). The spectral was recorded by averaging 64 recordings and at a resolution of 4 $\\mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 }$ with transmission mode from 4000 cm<sup>−1</sup> to $4 0 0 \\mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 }$ . Introduction\n[原文]\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the differences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H···O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds differed at various refining stages.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining\n[原文]\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers."

PyMuPDF结构81块 · 要点 3/3；边界 2/2

论文观察到软木和硬木纤维中三类氢键的峰位在整个打浆过程中几乎保持不变，因此氢键能量和氢键距离基本不变。 [1]
同一研究的摘要指出，打浆后晶型、氢键距离和各类氢键的能量几乎不变，但结晶指数、微晶尺寸和不同氢键的含量随打浆发生变化。 [7]
所以不能由氢键能量和距离基本不变推出打浆对氢键网络基本没影响；该结果只反映局部氢键参数稳定，而不同氢键的含量和网络组成仍可能改变。 [1] [7]

Therefore, taking derivative of the OH bands can improve\nthe resolution of various H-bonds. Normally, 3580–3550 cm−1 is for free OH(2) and OH(6), 3455–3410 cm−1\nis for O(2)H···O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds, 3375–3340 cm−1 is for O(3)H···O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds,\nand 3310–3230 cm−1 is for O(6)H···O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds in cellulose I [31,32].",
      "Polymers 2020, 12, 2912 2 of 14\nﬁrst and then decreased with the degree of reﬁning for hardwood bleached kraft pulp ﬁbers [11] or\nfor unbleached eucalyptus ﬁbers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially\nﬂuctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating ﬂuctuation with PFI reﬁning for\ntobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identiﬁed a clear trend, but the results\nwere that the crystallinity varied during PFI reﬁnement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in\ncrystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during\nPFI reﬁning.\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure,\ncan be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl\ngroups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding\ndistance during deligniﬁcation [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used\nto study the diﬀerences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal\nregion [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during\nPFI reﬁning, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of\neucalyptus ﬁbers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that\nthe H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions\nof the content of certain H-bonds diﬀered at various reﬁning stages.\n\nThere is still a lack of literature on the eﬀects of PFI reﬁnement on the H-bonding network.\nParticularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of\nfurther study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of\nH-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, ﬂexibility,\nand ﬁbrillation of cellulosic ﬁbers during PFI reﬁnement. Therefore, this work explored the eﬀects\nof PFI reﬁnement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of\nH-bonds for softwood pulp ﬁbers and hardwood pulp ﬁbers. Attempts were made in order to establish\nthe correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.",
      "polymers\nArticle\nProbing Eﬀect of Papirindustriens Forskningsinstitut\n(PFI) Reﬁning on Aggregation Structure of Cellulose:\nCrystal Packing and Hydrogen-Bonding Network\nKunpeng Li, Lihong Zhao * and Beihai He\nState Key Laboratory of Pulp and Paper Engineering, South China University of Technology, 381 Wushan Rd.,\nTianhe District, Guangzhou 510640, China; felikp@mail.scut.edu.cn (K.L.); ppebhhe@scut.edu.cn (B.H.)\n* Correspondence: zhaolh@scut.edu.cn\nReceived: 17 November 2020; Accepted: 2 December 2020; Published: 4 December 2020\nAbstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that aﬀects the properties of cellulosic\nﬁbers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) reﬁning on the\nmolecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between\nthe crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic ﬁbers. The results showed that\nthe polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost\nunchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed\nwith reﬁning. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds was signiﬁcantly\ncorrelated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson\ncorrelation coeﬃcient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood ﬁbers and 0.889 (p < 0.05)\nfor hardwood ﬁbers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling,\nand ﬁbrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds\nplay an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.\n\nKeywords: natural cellulosic ﬁbers; mechanical reﬁning; Crystallinity; Crystallite size;\nHydrogen bonds",
      "9. Xu, H.; Li, B.; Mu, X.; Yu, G.; Liu, C.; Zhang, Y.; Wang, H. Quantitative characterization of the impact of pulp\nreﬁning on enzymatic sacchariﬁcation of the alkaline pretreated corn stover. Bioresour. Technol. 2014, 169,\n19–26. [CrossRef] [PubMed]\n\n10. Gao, W.; Xiang, Z.; Chen, K.; Yang, R.; Yang, F. Eﬀect of depth beating on the ﬁber properties and enzymatic\nsacchariﬁcation eﬃciency of softwood kraft pulp. Carbohydr. Polym. 2015, 127, 400–406. [CrossRef]"

PFI2-021 · 阔叶木的O(3)H···O(5)分子内氢键相对含量，从4000转到12000转变化了多少个百分点？相对变化是百分之几？

参考答案与评分要点

由4000转33.06%降到12000转29.28%：减少33.06−29.28=3.78个百分点；相对降幅3.78/33.06×100%≈11.43%。含量是FT-IR拟合峰面积占比，不是绝对氢键数量；该区间结果为按表计算，正文未直接给出。

从4000转到12000转，阔叶木O(3)H···O(5)分子内氢键相对含量下降3.78个百分点。 [3]
以4000转时的33.06%为基准，从4000转到12000转的相对变化约为-11.43%，即相对下降约11.43%。 [3]

Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nFor the content of O(6)H···O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the trend can be divided into two stages, as shown in Table 2a. It decreased by 7.72% from 28.23% to 26.05% as refining from 0r to 4000 r and then increased by 9.14% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by a decrease of 17.13%, with the revolutions increasing from 8000 r to 16,000 r. Regarding the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, the trend was almost similar to that of softwood fibers, except for a small increase of 0.45% from 8000 r to 12,000 r (in Table 2b). On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\n Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1).",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \\mathrm { H } \\cdots \\mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nIn the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood fiber, the trend of content can be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend in general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the breakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and higher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose more accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups, which makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H···O(6) or O(6)H···O(3′)H-bonds. Thus although there is the formation of free OH(2) and OH(6) during fibrillation, the content of the free OH(2) and OH(6) might disease; meanwhile, the content of the O(6)H···O(3′) or the O(2)H···O(6) H-bonds might increase upon drying.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3.       "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.",

      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nFor the content of O(6)H···O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the trend can be divided into two stages, as shown in Table 2a. It decreased by 7.72% from 28.23% to 26.05% as refining from 0r to 4000 r and then increased by 9.14% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by a decrease of 17.13%, with the revolutions increasing from 8000 r to 16,000 r. Regarding the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, the trend was almost similar to that of softwood fibers, except for a small increase of 0.45% from 8000 r to 12,000 r (in Table 2b). On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\n Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1).",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \\mathrm { H } \\cdots \\mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nIn the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood fiber, the trend of content can be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend in general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the breakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and higher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose more accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups, which makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H···O(6) or O(6)H···O(3′)H-bonds. Thus although there is the formation of free OH(2) and OH(6) during fibrillation, the content of the free OH(2) and OH(6) might disease; meanwhile, the content of the O(6)H···O(3′) or the O(2)H···O(6) H-bonds might increase upon drying.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.4. Correlation between CI and Content of Inter-Molecular H-Bonds during PFI Refining\n[原文]\nSimilar to the CI-XI, the content of O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds decreased first and then had an increase, followed by a decline for the two fibers (as shown in Figure 8a,b). Besides, the Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated between the content of H-bonds and the CI-XI. It was 0.912 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. The similar trends in the content of the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds and the CI-XI might be because that the crystalline region has a higher content of O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds when compared with the amorphous regions, as illustrated in Figure 9 [35].",

      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.",

阔叶木的 O(3)H···O(5) 分子内氢键相对含量在 4000 r 时为 33.06%，在 12000 r 时为 29.28%。 [3]
从 4000 r 到 12000 r，该相对含量变化为 29.28% − 33.06% = −3.78 个百分点，即下降 3.78 个百分点。 [3]
以 4000 r 的 33.06% 为基准，相对变化为 (−3.78 / 33.06) × 100% ≈ −11.43%，即相对下降约 11.43%。 [3]

      "Polymers 2020, 12, 2912 9 of 14\n\nFigure 7. The deconvoluted FT-IR spectra of softwood ﬁbers at various revolutions: (a) 0 r, (b) 4000 r,\n(c) 8000 r, (d) 12,000 r, and (e) 16,000 r.\nFor the content of O(6)H· · · O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds of softwood ﬁber, the trend can be\ndivided into two stages, as shown in Table 2a. It decreased by 7.72% from 28.23% to 26.05% as reﬁning\nfrom 0r to 4000 r and then increased by 9.14% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by a decrease of 17.13%,\nwith the revolutions increasing from 8000 r to 16,000 r. Regarding the O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds of\nhardwood ﬁber, the trend was almost similar to that of softwood ﬁbers, except for a small increase of\n0.45% from 8000 r to 12,000 r (in Table 2b). On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds\nfor softwood ﬁbers and hardwood ﬁbers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively.\nThe decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical\naction of PFI reﬁning, which was closely related to internal and external ﬁbrillation (as seen in\nSection 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also",
      "Polymers 2020, 12, 2912 10 of 14\nthe formation of O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI\n(as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the ﬂexibility of cellulosic ﬁbers, due to the higher mobility\nof molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of ﬁbers (as seen in Section 3.1).\nAs to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood ﬁber, the content had a growth\nof 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of reﬁning from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight\ndecrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of reﬁning.\nOverall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood ﬁbers, which ﬁrst increased and then had a\ndecrease, followed by a growth. During the whole reﬁning, the amount of O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds for\nsoftwood ﬁbers and hardwood ﬁbers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%,\nrespectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only\nless breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the\namorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important\nrole in the cellulose stiﬀness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose\nstiﬀness [33,34].\n\nIn the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood ﬁber, the trend of content\ncan be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of reﬁning\nfrom 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26%\nin the last reﬁning stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood ﬁber, it increased\nﬁrstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both ﬁbers, the content of\nO(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of reﬁning from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to\nthe fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than\nO(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.\nAs to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend\nin general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the\nbreakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and\nhigher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose\nmore accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber,\nthe number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions\nincreasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to\n12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups,\nwhich makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H···O(6) or O(6)H···O(3′)H-bonds. Thus although\nthere is the formation of free OH(2) and OH(6) during fibrillation, the content of the free OH(2) and OH(6)\nmight disease; meanwhile, the content of the O(6)H···O(3′) or the O(2)H···O(6) H-bonds might increase\nupon drying.\n\n3.4. Correlation between CI and Content of Inter-Molecular H-Bonds during PFI Reﬁning\nSimilar to the CI-XI, the content of O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds decreased ﬁrst and then had an increase,\nfollowed by a decline for the two ﬁbers (as shown in Figure 8a,b). Besides, the Pearson correlation\ncoeﬃcients were calculated between the content of H-bonds and the CI-XI. It was 0.912 (p < 0.05)\nfor softwood ﬁbers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood ﬁbers, respectively. The similar trends in the\ncontent of the O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds and the CI-XI might be because that the crystalline region has a\nhigher content of O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds when compared with the amorphous regions, as illustrated\nin Figure 9 [35].",

      "Polymers 2020, 12, 2912 2 of 14\nﬁrst and then decreased with the degree of reﬁning for hardwood bleached kraft pulp ﬁbers [11] or\nfor unbleached eucalyptus ﬁbers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially\nﬂuctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating ﬂuctuation with PFI reﬁning for\ntobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identiﬁed a clear trend, but the results\nwere that the crystallinity varied during PFI reﬁnement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in\ncrystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during\nPFI reﬁning.\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure,\ncan be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl\ngroups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding\ndistance during deligniﬁcation [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used\nto study the diﬀerences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal\nregion [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during\nPFI reﬁning, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of\neucalyptus ﬁbers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that\nthe H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions\nof the content of certain H-bonds diﬀered at various reﬁning stages.\n\nThere is still a lack of literature on the eﬀects of PFI reﬁnement on the H-bonding network.\nParticularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of\nfurther study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of\nH-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, ﬂexibility,\nand ﬁbrillation of cellulosic ﬁbers during PFI reﬁnement. Therefore, this work explored the eﬀects\nof PFI reﬁnement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of\nH-bonds for softwood pulp ﬁbers and hardwood pulp ﬁbers. Attempts were made in order to establish\nthe correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.",

      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nIn the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood fiber, the trend of content can be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend in general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the breakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and higher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose more accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups, which makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H···O(6) or O(6)H···O(3′)H-bonds. Thus although there is the formation of free OH(2) and OH(6) during fibrillation, the content of the free OH(2) and OH(6) might disease; meanwhile, the content of the O(6)H···O(3′) or the O(2)H···O(6) H-bonds might increase upon drying.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.4. Correlation between CI and Content of Inter-Molecular H-Bonds during PFI Refining\n[原文]\nSimilar to the CI-XI, the content of O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds decreased first and then had an increase, followed by a decline for the two fibers (as shown in Figure 8a,b). Besides, the Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated between the content of H-bonds and the CI-XI. It was 0.912 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. The similar trends in the content of the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds and the CI-XI might be because that the crystalline region has a higher content of O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds when compared with the amorphous regions, as illustrated in Figure 9 [35].",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.4. Correlation between CI and Content of Inter-Molecular H-Bonds during PFI Refining\n[原文]\nFigure 8. The trend of the CI-XI, the CI-XA, and the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds: (a) softwood fibers andd fibers. (b) hardwood fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.4. Correlation between CI and Content of Inter-Molecular H-Bonds during PFI Refining\n[原文]\nFigure 9. The illustration of a two-phase structure of cellulose.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.4. Correlation between CI and Content of Inter-Molecular H-Bonds during PFI Refining\n[原文]\nThe correlation between the CI-XI and the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds or the free OH(2) and OH(6) was poor for the following reasons. The free OH groups are easier for forming the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds as opposed to the O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds in the amorphous region, because the distance between adjacent glucose units in a cellulosic molecular chain is closer than between the glucose units in the adjacent molecular chain (as shown in Figure 9). Accordingly, when compared with the content of O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds, there was less difference in the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds or the free OH groups between the crystalline region and amorphous region, which sometimes made the content of the two bonds not change much in regards to the crystallinity. The O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds is stable, as mentioned above. It was presumed to change little as crystallinity changed during PFI refining. Hence, the correlation between O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds and the CI-XI was not discussed in the present study.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4.
