XRD Analysis\n[原文]\nThe crystallinity of pretreated fibers was determined by a Shimadzu XRD 7000S (Shimadzu, Kyoto, Japan), while using Cu-Ka radiation. The samples were scanned at 40 kV and 30 mA in a 2θ range of $4 { - } 4 0 ^ { \\circ }$ at 1<sup>◦</sup>/min. It is well known that two polymorphs, cellulose Iα and Iβ, are present in native cellulose; for clarity, all of the reflections indexed here are on the Iβ lattice. Before analysis, the experimental data is nine point smoothed with Savitzky–Golay algorithm. The two types of CI values were obtained from peak intensity method (CI − XI) and peak fitting (CI-XA), respectively. The CI − XI was calculated as in Equation (2) [19].\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.4. XRD Analysis\n[原文]\n$$\nC I - X I = \\frac {\\left(I _ {2 0 0} - I _ {a m}\\right)}{I _ {2 0 0}} \\times 1 0 0 \\%\\tag{2}\n$$",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nIn the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood fiber, the trend of content can be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend in general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the breakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and higher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose more accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups, which makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H···O(6) or O(6)H···O(3′)H-bonds. Thus although there is the formation of free OH(2) and OH(6) during fibrillation, the content of the free OH(2) and OH(6) might disease; meanwhile, the content of the O(6)H···O(3′) or the O(2)H···O(6) H-bonds might increase upon drying.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.4. Correlation between CI and Content of Inter-Molecular H-Bonds during PFI Refining\n[原文]\nSimilar to the CI-XI, the content of O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds decreased first and then had an increase, followed by a decline for the two fibers (as shown in Figure 8a,b). Besides, the Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated between the content of H-bonds and the CI-XI. It was 0.912 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. The similar trends in the content of the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds and the CI-XI might be because that the crystalline region has a higher content of O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds when compared with the amorphous regions, as illustrated in Figure 9 [35]."

论文仅在图3中以随打浆转数变化的曲线形式给出抗张指数、零距抗张指数和湿纸幅强度，而没有给出逐次平行实验的原始数值。 [6]
方法部分仅说明干纸抗张强度按TAPPI T494测试，未提供针叶木8000转组的平行实验明细。 [1]
在所提供的证据中，未见针叶木8000转组干纸抗张指数的每次平行实验原始数据。 [1] [6]

文中8000转对应的表格数据为结晶度与晶粒尺寸，并非干纸抗张指数。 [4]

The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing\nﬁbrillation and ﬁnes during PFI reﬁning, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood\nﬁber had a more signiﬁcant increase when compared to that of hardwood ﬁber. It is for that ﬁber\nlength plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in\ncharacterizing the tensile strength of ﬁbers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that\nPFI reﬁning did not reduce ﬁber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24].\nThe above results showed that PFI reﬁning improved the extent of ﬁbrillation (especially the internal\nﬁbrillation), the swelling of ﬁbers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile\nstrength of ﬁbers.\n\nFigure 3. The rheological analysis of wet sheets, the tensile strength of dry sheets, and the ﬁber strength\nfor unreﬁned and reﬁned samples: (a) softwood ﬁbers and (b) hardwood ﬁbers.\n\n3.2. Eﬀect of PFI Reﬁning on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\nThe cellulose polymorph of these two ﬁbers had no change during PFI treatment, which illustrates\nthat the PFI reﬁning is a relatively mild mechanical treatment, as the results of XRD in Online Resource\n(Figures S1 and S2) show. In general, the CI-XI and the CI-XA of softwood ﬁbers showed a reduction\nof 4.66% and 15.47%, respectively, and those of hardwood ﬁbers decreased by 2.65% and 19.4%,\nrespectively, as can be seen in Figure 4 and Table 1. The value of the CI-XI was remarkably higher than\nthe CI-XA, which might be caused by the over-ﬁtting of amorphous contribution in the analysis of\nCI-XA. However, the CI-XI and the CI-XA were correlated signiﬁcantly for both softwood ﬁbers and\nhardwood ﬁbers, with a correlation coeﬃcient of 0.919 (p < 0.05) for softwood ﬁbers and 0.925 (p < 0.05)\nfor hardwood ﬁbers, respectively, which is consistent with the report of Ahvenainen et al. [25]."

PFI2-027 · 这篇论文对干纸抗张性能有什么结论？另外请给出同一批样品的耐破指数和撕裂指数精确数据。

参考答案与评分要点

可回答部分：作者报告PFI打浆提高纸页抗张性能，并将其与细纤维化及细小纤维增加联系。无法回答部分：当前正文没有报告同批样品耐破指数和撕裂指数的精确数据，需要相应试验资料，不能由抗张结果直接换算。

表格行检索＋关联补全 · 要点 2/2；边界 2/2

PFI精磨提高干纸抗张强度，其主要原因是精磨过程中纤维细纤维化（尤其内部细纤维化）和细组分增加。 [1]
零距抗张指数结果表明PFI精磨没有降低纤维自身强度，因此纸页抗张强度的提高并非以牺牲纤维强度为代价。 [1]
所提供的证据仅在第3.1节报告抗张指数、零距抗张指数和湿纸幅强度等，未给出同一批样品的耐破指数和撕裂指数精确数据，故无法从这些证据中提供该数据。 [1]

      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions\n[原文]\nThe results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general.       "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining\n[原文]\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. 解析修复95块 · 要点 2/2；边界 2/2

该论文认为PFI打浆提高了干纸页的抗张强度，主要原因是打浆过程中细纤维化和细组分增加。 [1]
零-span抗张指数结果表明PFI打浆未降低纤维强度，这与Kouko等的报道一致。 [1]
湿纸幅强度方面，软木纤维的提高比硬木纤维更显著，原因在于纤维长度对湿纸幅强度起重要作用。 [1]
在提供的证据中，力学性能相关结果只报告了抗张指数/干纸抗张强度、零-span抗张指数和湿纸幅强度，未报告耐破指数或撕裂指数的精确数据。 [1] [3]

      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions\n[原文]\nThe results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. PyMuPDF结构81块 · 要点 2/2；边界 2/2

PFI精磨带来的抗张强度增量主要来自精磨过程中不断增加的细纤维化与细小组分。 [1]
零-span抗张指数结果表明PFI精磨没有降低纤维强度，这与Kouko等人的报道一致。 [1]
上述结果表明，PFI精磨提高了细纤维化（尤其是内部细纤维化）程度、纤维润胀以及纸页抗张强度，而纤维的抗张强度并未下降。 [1]
所提供的证据仅涉及抗张强度、零-span抗张强度、湿纸幅强度等测试，未包含耐破指数与撕裂指数的任何数值，故无法给出这两个指标的精确数据。 [1] [4]

The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers."

  "task_id": "PFI2-027",
  "answer": "PFI精磨带来的抗张强度增量主要来自精磨过程中不断增加的细纤维化与细小组分。 [1]\n零-span抗张指数结果表明PFI精磨没有降低纤维强度，这与Kouko等人的报道一致。 [1]\n上述结果表明，PFI精磨提高了细纤维化（尤其是内部细纤维化）程度、纤维润胀以及纸页抗张强度，而纤维的抗张强度并未下降。 [1]\n所提供的证据仅涉及抗张强度、零-span抗张强度、湿纸幅强度等测试，未包含耐破指数与撕裂指数的任何数值，故无法给出这两个指标的精确数据。 [1] [4]",

      "text": "Figure 2. The beating degree and Water Retention Value (WRV) for the unreﬁned and reﬁned samples:\n(a) softwood ﬁbers and (b) hardwood ﬁbers.\nIn Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a\nfunction of the reﬁning revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing\nﬁbrillation and ﬁnes during PFI reﬁning, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood\nﬁber had a more signiﬁcant increase when compared to that of hardwood ﬁber. It is for that ﬁber\nlength plays an essential role in wet–web strength. [24].\nThe above results showed that PFI reﬁning improved the extent of ﬁbrillation (especially the internal\nﬁbrillation), the swelling of ﬁbers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile\nstrength of ﬁbers.\n\nFigure 3. The rheological analysis of wet sheets, the tensile strength of dry sheets, and the ﬁber strength\nfor unreﬁned and reﬁned samples: (a) softwood ﬁbers and (b) hardwood ﬁbers.\n\n3.2. Eﬀect of PFI Reﬁning on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\nThe cellulose polymorph of these two ﬁbers had no change during PFI treatment, which illustrates\nthat the PFI reﬁning is a relatively mild mechanical treatment, as the results of XRD in Online Resource\n(Figures S1 and S2) show.       "text": "2.1. PFI Reﬁning\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp ﬁbers were obtained from\nZhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). 表格行检索＋关联补全 · 要点 2/2；边界 2/2

所给证据材料仅涉及 Li-2020 PFI refining 论文，包括其结论、方法、引言和参考文献。 [1] [2] [3] [4] [5]
该 PFI 论文结论指出，PFI refining 的纤丝化与纤维超分子结构变化相关，且 CI-XI 与 O(6)H···O(3)’ 氢键含量在软木和硬木纤维中呈显著正相关。 [1]
该论文还指出，结晶尺寸、结晶度和各种氢键含量在 PFI refining 过程中总体变化不大。 [1]
由于所给证据未包含第二篇论文的数据，不能据此比较两篇论文的全部实验数据，也不能给出两篇共同结论。 [1]

Introduction\n[原文]\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the differences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H···O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds differed at various refining stages.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining\n[原文]\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.",

Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.",

      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions\n[原文]\nThe results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. 解析修复95块 · 要点 2/2；边界 2/2

所给证据中可提取的实验结论来自 Li-2020 PFI 论文，涉及软木纤维和硬木纤维在 PFI 精磨过程中的纤丝化、结晶与氢键变化。 [1]
PFI 精磨过程中纤维的纤丝化及性能与超分子结构变化相关。 [1]
对软木纤维和硬木纤维，CI-XI 与 O(6)H···O(3’) 氢键含量在 PFI 精磨过程中呈显著正相关。 [1]
总体上，微晶尺寸、结晶度及各类氢键含量变化不大。 [1]
作者认为 PFI 精磨是一种对超分子结构破坏相对较小的优良机械纤丝化处理。 [1]
在现有证据下，只能报告上述 PFI 论文结论，不能给出其与《Non-Wood Fibers: Relationships of Fiber Properties with Pulp Properties》全部实验数据的共同结论。 [1]

  "answer": "所给证据中可提取的实验结论来自 Li-2020 PFI 论文，涉及软木纤维和硬木纤维在 PFI 精磨过程中的纤丝化、结晶与氢键变化。 [1]\nPFI 精磨过程中纤维的纤丝化及性能与超分子结构变化相关。 [1]\n对软木纤维和硬木纤维，CI-XI 与 O(6)H···O(3’) 氢键含量在 PFI 精磨过程中呈显著正相关。 [1]\n总体上，微晶尺寸、结晶度及各类氢键含量变化不大。 [1]\n作者认为 PFI 精磨是一种对超分子结构破坏相对较小的优良机械纤丝化处理。 [1]\n在现有证据下，只能报告上述 PFI 论文结论，不能给出其与《Non-Wood Fibers: Relationships of Fiber Properties with Pulp Properties》全部实验数据的共同结论。 [1]",

      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the differences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H···O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds differed at various refining stages.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining\n[原文]\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.",

      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining."

PyMuPDF结构81块 · 要点 2/2；边界 2/2

所给证据中的Li-2020 PFI论文研究了PFI精磨对纤维素聚集结构、晶胞堆积和氢键网络的影响，但所给证据未包含《Non-Wood Fibers: Relationships of Fiber Properties with Pulp Properties》的实验数据，因此无法比较两篇论文的全部实验数据或给出两篇共同结论。 [4]
PFI论文用PFI精磨处理漂白软木和硬木硫酸盐浆，精磨转数为0、4000、8000、12000和16000转。 [2]
PFI论文报告O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键含量与CI显著正相关，软木纤维Pearson相关系数为0.888，硬木纤维为0.889，p<0.05。 [4]
PFI论文报告PFI精磨后晶型、氢键距离和各氢键的氢键能几乎不变，而结晶指数、微晶尺寸和各类氢键含量随精磨发生变化。 [4]
PFI论文认为PFI精磨是一种对超分子结构破坏相对较小的良好机械纤丝化处理。 [1]

      "text": "polymers\nArticle\nProbing Eﬀect of Papirindustriens Forskningsinstitut\n(PFI) Reﬁning on Aggregation Structure of Cellulose:\nCrystal Packing and Hydrogen-Bonding Network\nKunpeng Li, Lihong Zhao * and Beihai He\nState Key Laboratory of Pulp and Paper Engineering, South China University of Technology, 381 Wushan Rd.,\nTianhe District, Guangzhou 510640, China; felikp@mail.scut.edu.cn (K.L.); ppebhhe@scut.edu.cn (B.H.)\n* Correspondence: zhaolh@scut.edu.cn\nReceived: 17 November 2020; Accepted: 2 December 2020; Published: 4 December 2020\nAbstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that aﬀects the properties of cellulosic\nﬁbers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) reﬁning on the\nmolecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between\nthe crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic ﬁbers. The results showed that\nthe polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost\nunchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed\nwith reﬁning. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds was signiﬁcantly\ncorrelated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson\ncorrelation coeﬃcient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood ﬁbers and 0.889 (p < 0.05)\nfor hardwood ﬁbers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling,\nand ﬁbrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds\nplay an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.\n\nKeywords: natural cellulosic ﬁbers; mechanical reﬁning; Crystallinity; Crystallite size;\nHydrogen bonds\n\n1. Introduction\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired\nphysical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic ﬁbers. Therein,\nPapirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) reﬁning is the most common laboratory reﬁner in order to\nimprove the inter-ﬁber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-ﬁbrillated\nor nano-ﬁbrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main eﬀects of PFI reﬁning on ﬁbers are: (i) internal\nﬁbrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of ﬁber wall; (ii) external ﬁbrillation—peeling of\nﬁbrils from the ﬁber surface while remaining attached; (iii) ﬁber shortening—ﬁber cutting due to\nshearing action, and (iv) ﬁnes formation—primary ﬁnes come from ray cells and parenchyma cells\nand microﬁbrils that are caused by ﬁber shortening or external ﬁbrillation. Moreover, the PFI reﬁning\ncould be adopted to obtain a higher internal ﬁbrillation than other laboratory reﬁners [1]. These eﬀects\nof the PFI reﬁning on cellulosic ﬁbers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the ﬂexibility, and the\ninter-ﬁber bonding capacity of ﬁbers. It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and\nproperties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during reﬁning [7,8].\n\nThere are some diﬀerent conclusions regarding to the eﬀects of PFI reﬁning on crystallinity of\ncellulose, not like that of ball milling, which eﬀectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment\nprogresses. Two pulp\nﬁbers were separately reﬁned in a PFI reﬁner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and\nat 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an\nincreasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79◦SR, were obtained for softwood ﬁbers and 0,\n26, 40, 57, and 70◦SR were obtained for hardwood ﬁbers.\n\n2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets\nThe ﬁnes content, weighted mean length, and macro-ﬁbrillation index of each sample were\ndetermined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of\ndry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT\n12914-2008, respectively. [CrossRef]",
      "polymers\nArticle\nProbing Eﬀect of Papirindustriens Forskningsinstitut\n(PFI) Reﬁning on Aggregation Structure of Cellulose:\nCrystal Packing and Hydrogen-Bonding Network\nKunpeng Li, Lihong Zhao * and Beihai He\nState Key Laboratory of Pulp and Paper Engineering, South China University of Technology, 381 Wushan Rd.,\nTianhe District, Guangzhou 510640, China; felikp@mail.scut.edu.cn (K.L.); ppebhhe@scut.edu.cn (B.H.)\n* Correspondence: zhaolh@scut.edu.cn\nReceived: 17 November 2020; Accepted: 2 December 2020; Published: 4 December 2020\nAbstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that aﬀects the properties of cellulosic\nﬁbers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) reﬁning on the\nmolecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between\nthe crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic ﬁbers. The results showed that\nthe polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost\nunchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed\nwith reﬁning. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds was signiﬁcantly\ncorrelated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson\ncorrelation coeﬃcient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood ﬁbers and 0.889 (p < 0.05)\nfor hardwood ﬁbers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling,\nand ﬁbrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds\nplay an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.\n\nKeywords: natural cellulosic ﬁbers; mechanical reﬁning; Crystallinity; Crystallite size;\nHydrogen bonds\n\n1. Introduction\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired\nphysical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic ﬁbers. Therein,\nPapirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) reﬁning is the most common laboratory reﬁner in order to\nimprove the inter-ﬁber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-ﬁbrillated\nor nano-ﬁbrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main eﬀects of PFI reﬁning on ﬁbers are: (i) internal\nﬁbrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of ﬁber wall; (ii) external ﬁbrillation—peeling of\nﬁbrils from the ﬁber surface while remaining attached; (iii) ﬁber shortening—ﬁber cutting due to\nshearing action, and (iv) ﬁnes formation—primary ﬁnes come from ray cells and parenchyma cells\nand microﬁbrils that are caused by ﬁber shortening or external ﬁbrillation. Moreover, the PFI reﬁning\ncould be adopted to obtain a higher internal ﬁbrillation than other laboratory reﬁners [1]. These eﬀects\nof the PFI reﬁning on cellulosic ﬁbers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the ﬂexibility, and the\ninter-ﬁber bonding capacity of ﬁbers. It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and\nproperties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during reﬁning [7,8].\n\nThere are some diﬀerent conclusions regarding to the eﬀects of PFI reﬁning on crystallinity of\ncellulose, not like that of ball milling, which eﬀectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment\nprogresses. PFI2-029 · 本文已经训练好的纸张抗张预测模型，其验证集R²和RMSE是多少？请给出最佳模型名称。

参考答案与评分要点

当前正文没有报告训练好的纸张抗张预测模型、验证集R²或RMSE，也没有最佳预测模型名称。文中CI与氢键的Pearson相关系数，以及FT-IR峰拟合r²，都不能冒充纸张抗张预测性能。

表格行检索＋关联补全 · 要点 1/1；边界 2/2

所提供证据对应的文献研究的是 PFI 精磨对软木浆和硬木浆纤维结晶度、晶粒尺寸及氢键网络的影响，属于实验表征研究而非建模研究 [1] [3]
该研究只测试了干纸页抗张强度、湿纸幅强度和零-span 抗张强度等指标随精磨转数的变化，并未建立或训练抗张强度预测模型 [2]
文中出现的 r² 数值（如软木浆 0.9995、硬木浆 0.9990 等）是羟基谱带非线性分峰拟合的决定系数，不是抗张预测模型验证集的 R² [5] [8]
由于证据中不存在该预测模型，其验证集 R²、RMSE 及最佳模型名称均无法从所给材料中确定 [1] [2]

      "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining\n[原文]\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets\n[原文]\nThe fines content, weighted mean length, and macro-fibrillation index of each sample were determined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of dry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT 12914-2008, respectively. The zero-span tensile strength was tested with the Z-Span 2400 apparatus (Pulmac International Co. Ltd., Montpelier, VT, USA), according to the standard ISO 15361.",

The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\n[原文]\nIn Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.1. The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\n[原文]\nFigure 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Effect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe cellulose polymorph of these two fibers had no change during PFI treatment, which illustrates that the PFI refining is a relatively mild mechanical treatment, as the results of XRD in Online Resource (Figures S1 and S2) show. In general, the CI-XI and the CI-XA of softwood fibers showed a reduction of 4.66% and 15.47%, respectively, and those of hardwood fibers decreased by 2.65% and 19.4%, respectively, as can be seen in Figure 4 and Table 1. The value of the CI-XI was remarkably higher than the CI-XA, which might be caused by the over-fitting of amorphous contribution in the analysis of CI-XA. However, the CI-XI and the CI-XA were correlated significantly for both softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, with a correlation coefficient of 0.919 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.925 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively, which is consistent with the report of Ahvenainen et al. Conclusions\n[原文]\nThe results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. It decreased by 7.72% from 28.23% to 26.05% as refining from 0r to 4000 r and then increased by 9.14% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by a decrease of 17.13%, with the revolutions increasing from 8000 r to 16,000 r. Regarding the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, the trend was almost similar to that of softwood fibers, except for a small increase of 0.45% from 8000 r to 12,000 r (in Table 2b). On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). 表中出现的 r² 数值是三种氢键和游离 OH 的拟合结果，并非纸张抗张预测模型的验证集 R²。 [5]

      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining\n[原文]\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets\n[原文]\nThe fines content, weighted mean length, and macro-fibrillation index of each sample were determined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of dry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT 12914-2008, respectively. The zero-span tensile strength was tested with the Z-Span 2400 apparatus (Pulmac International Co. Ltd., Montpelier, VT, USA), according to the standard ISO 15361.",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.1. The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\n[原文]\nFigure 2. The beating degree and Water Retention Value (WRV) for the unrefined and refined samples: (a) softwood fibers and (b) hardwood fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.1. The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\n[原文]\nIn Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.1. The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\n[原文]\nFigure 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Effect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe cellulose polymorph of these two fibers had no change during PFI treatment, which illustrates that the PFI refining is a relatively mild mechanical treatment, as the results of XRD in Online Resource (Figures S1 and S2) show. In general, the CI-XI and the CI-XA of softwood fibers showed a reduction of 4.66% and 15.47%, respectively, and those of hardwood fibers decreased by 2.65% and 19.4%, respectively, as can be seen in Figure 4 and Table 1. The value of the CI-XI was remarkably higher than the CI-XA, which might be caused by the over-fitting of amorphous contribution in the analysis of CI-XA. However, the CI-XI and the CI-XA were correlated significantly for both softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, with a correlation coefficient of 0.919 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.925 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively, which is consistent with the report of Ahvenainen et al. [25].",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions\n[原文]\nThe results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. XRD Analysis\nThe crystallinity of pretreated ﬁbers was determined by a Shimadzu XRD 7000S (Shimadzu,\nKyoto, Japan), while using Cu-Ka radiation. The samples were scanned at 40 kV and 30 mA in a 2θ\nrange of 4–40◦at 1◦/min. It is well known that two polymorphs, cellulose Iα and Iβ, are present in\nnative cellulose; for clarity, all of the reﬂections indexed here are on the Iβ lattice. Before analysis,\nthe experimental data is nine point smoothed with Savitzky–Golay algorithm. The two types of CI\nvalues were obtained from peak intensity method (CI −XI) and peak ﬁtting (CI-XA), respectively.\nThe CI −XI was calculated as in Equation (2) [19].\n(I200 −Iam) CI −XI = × 100% (2)\nI200\nwhere I200 is the maximum diﬀraction intensity value of the (200) lattice plane between the scattering\nangles of 2θ = 22◦and 23◦, and Iam is the minimum diﬀraction intensity of amorphous fraction between\n2θ = 18◦and 19◦.\nAll of the XRD diﬀractograms were smoothed with the Savitzky–Golay algorithm and\nbaseline-corrected with linear ﬁt function. Subsequently, the baseline-corrected diﬀractograms\nwere deconvoluted with the Pearson VII function. The value of the CI-XA equals the area percentage\noccupied by crystalline peaks over the total area of the diﬀraction pattern [20]. In addition, the crystallite\nsize was calculated by the widely used Scherrer Equation (3) [21]:\nk × λ\nL = (3)\n(β × cos θ)\nwhere L is the size that is perpendicular to the lattice plane, k is a constant that depends on the crystal\nshape (0.89), λ is the wavelength of the incident beam in the diﬀraction experiment (0.154 nm), β is the\nfull width at half maximum of the diﬀraction peak, and θ is the Bragg’s angle. In general, the values of\nthe calculated crystallite sizes might be lower than that of the real crystallite sizes, because the peak\nbroadening from the instrumental factors was not considered [22].\n\n2.5. FT-IR Analysis\nTHE FT-IR spectra were recorded on solid samples in KBr pellets by means of an FT-IR Bruker\nVertex 70 spectrometer (Karlsruhe, Germany). Unreﬁned and reﬁned ﬁbers were smashed into powder\nbetween 40 and 60 mesh. Subsequently, the powder sample of each species (5 mg) was dispersed in a\nmatrix of highly pure KBr (500 mg). The spectral was recorded by averaging 64 recordings and at a\nresolution of 4 cm−1 with transmission mode from 4000 cm−1 to 400 cm−1.       "2. Methods\n\n2.1. PFI Reﬁning\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp ﬁbers were obtained from\nZhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI reﬁner\n(Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency\nof 10%, the gap between the opposite reﬁning plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were\n3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood ﬁbers and hardwood ﬁbers, respectively. The drainability was\ncharacterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp\nﬁbers were separately reﬁned in a PFI reﬁner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and\nat 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an\nincreasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79◦SR, were obtained for softwood ﬁbers and 0,\n26, 40, 57, and 70◦SR were obtained for hardwood ﬁbers.\n\n2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets\nThe ﬁnes content, weighted mean length, and macro-ﬁbrillation index of each sample were\ndetermined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of\ndry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT\n12914-2008, respectively. The zero-span tensile strength was tested with the Z-Span 2400 apparatus\n(Pulmac International Co. Ltd., Montpelier, VT, USA), according to the standard ISO 15361.",
      "Table 2. (a) The relative content of three H-bonds and the free OH for softwood ﬁbers through reﬁning.\n(b) The relative content of three H-bonds and the free OH for hardwood ﬁbers through reﬁning.\n(a)\nFree OH(2) Revolutions O(6)H· · · O(3′) O(3)H· · · O(5) O(2)H· · · O(6) r2\nand OH(6)\n0 28.23 28.44 31.40 11.93 0.9995\n4000 26.05 31.31 32.50 10.14 0.9995\n8000 28.43 30.86 25.87 14.84 0.9995\n12,000 26.68 32.58 25.49 15.25 0.9996\n16,000 23.56 34.92 29.38 12.14 0.9996\n(b)\nFree OH(2) Revolutions O(6)H· · · O(3′) O(3)H· · · O(5) O(2)H· · · O(6) r2\nand OH(6)\n0 26.55 29.09 30.04 14.32 0.9990\n4000 24.44 33.06 31.28 11.22 0.9991\n8000 26.89 29.81 28.99 14.31 0.9991\n12,000 27.01 29.28 27.40 16.31 0.9992\n16,000 24.98 31.65 29.85 13.52 0.9989",
      "Figure 2. The beating degree and Water Retention Value (WRV) for the unreﬁned and reﬁned samples:\n(a) softwood ﬁbers and (b) hardwood ﬁbers.\nIn Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a\nfunction of the reﬁning revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing\nﬁbrillation and ﬁnes during PFI reﬁning, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood\nﬁber had a more signiﬁcant increase when compared to that of hardwood ﬁber. It is for that ﬁber\nlength plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in\ncharacterizing the tensile strength of ﬁbers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that\nPFI reﬁning did not reduce ﬁber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24].\nThe above results showed that PFI reﬁning improved the extent of ﬁbrillation (especially the internal\nﬁbrillation), the swelling of ﬁbers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile\nstrength of ﬁbers.\n\nFigure 3. The rheological analysis of wet sheets, the tensile strength of dry sheets, and the ﬁber strength\nfor unreﬁned and reﬁned samples: (a) softwood ﬁbers and (b) hardwood ﬁbers.\n\n3.2. Eﬀect of PFI Reﬁning on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\nThe cellulose polymorph of these two ﬁbers had no change during PFI treatment, which illustrates\nthat the PFI reﬁning is a relatively mild mechanical treatment, as the results of XRD in Online Resource\n(Figures S1 and S2) show. The results were made on\nthe average spectrum that was obtained from ﬁve recordings.\nThe energy of the H-bonding EH for several OH stretching bands was calculated while using\nEquation (4) [13].\nνo −ν\nEH = (4)\nνo\nνo is the wavenumber corresponding to free OH groups (3650 cm−1), ν is the frequency (cm−1) of\nthe bonded OH groups, and k is a constant (1/k = 2.625 × 102 kJ).",
      "Polymers 2020, 12, 2912 7 of 14\n4.1.2 software). The result is consistent with the report of Haigler & Roberts [26], which shows that\nthere might be two microﬁbrils associated along part of their length.\n\nFigure 5. Cross-section model of cellulose crystallite for softwood ﬁbers and hardwood ﬁbers.\nIt is known that both the (110) and the (110) lattice plane are hydrophilic, and the (200)lattice\nplane is hydrophobic in cellulose Iβ (as Figure 5 shows). In addition, it is noticeable that the (110)\nplanes possess the highest theoretical roughness and accessibility to the hydrophilic groups in cellulose\nIβ [28]. Throughout the reﬁning of two pulp ﬁbers, the sizes perpendicular to (110) plane were more\nvolatile than the (110) plane and (200) plane, which is consistent with the report of Duchemin et al.,\nas shown in Table 1a,b [29]. It could be interpreted to be that water molecules were easier to permeate\nthrough the spaces between the hydrophilic (110) planes in paracrystalline region (hydration), and then\nit made these planes suﬀer more mechanical actions, so there was more adhesion (cocrystallization)\nand cleavage of cellulose chains created for (110) plane during PFI reﬁning.\nHowever, the crystallite size that was perpendicular to (200) lattice plane of two ﬁbers had an\nupward trend during PFI reﬁning. It could be explained in terms of coalescence of chains or some\ncrystallographic stacking of adjacent microﬁbrils, where the (200) planes were aligned upon drying [30].\n\nAdditionally, it was probably due to the weaker cleavage eﬀect on (200) lattice planes that was hard for\nwater molecules to penetrate.",
      "3.1. The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\nFor softwood ﬁbers and hardwood ﬁbers, the macro-ﬁbrillation index and the ﬁber length had\na downward trend, and the ﬁnes content has an upward trend for the softwood ﬁbers during PFI\nreﬁning, as can be seen in Figure 1. The macro-ﬁbrillation index and ﬁber length of softwood ﬁbers\nchanged signiﬁcantly. However, two parameters of hardwood ﬁbers had no signiﬁcant variations\nrelative to softwood ﬁbers. It might be because of the lower reﬁning pressure that was applied in\nhardwood ﬁbers. The macro-ﬁbrillation index characterizes external macro-ﬁbrillation. The results of\nﬁber morphology analysis showed that external ﬁbrillation increased with the reﬁning process. It is\nconsistent with the increasing speciﬁc surface area (as shown in Table S1 in Online Resource).\n\nFigure 1. The morphological analysis for the unreﬁned and reﬁned samples: (a) softwood ﬁbers and\n(b) hardwood ﬁbers.\nThe beating degree and the WRV had a signiﬁcant increment with increasing PFI reﬁning\nrevolutions, as can be seen in Figure 2. It is caused by the higher ﬁbrillation that produces the\nnew surface and more pores (as shown in Table S1 in Online Resource). The increase in swelling\ncharacterized by WRV makes the ﬁbers more compliant in transverse [1], which contributes to\nimproving the inter-ﬁber bonding strength of the ﬁber network. The results of ﬁber morphology\nanalysis and water retention value showing that the ﬁbrillation and the separation between ﬁbrils\nincrease with the reﬁning process."

PFI2-030 · 为什么阔叶木打浆后湿纸幅强度涨得比针叶木还多？

参考答案与评分要点

这个前提与论文不符：论文报告的是针叶木湿纸幅强度的增幅比阔叶木更明显，作者将其与纤维长度在湿纸幅强度中的重要作用联系起来。

表格行检索＋关联补全 · 要点 2/2；边界 2/2

文中比较针叶木与阔叶木时指出，针叶木湿纸幅强度的增幅比阔叶木更显著。 [3]
该文将湿纸幅强度的这一差异归因于纤维长度在湿纸幅强度中起关键作用。 [3]
PFI refining 提高拉伸强度主要归因于细纤维化和细小纤维的增加。 [3]
阔叶木的宏观细纤维化指数和纤维长度相对针叶木没有显著变化，这可能是因为对阔叶木施加了较低的磨浆压力。 [6]

Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.",

Effect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe cellulose polymorph of these two fibers had no change during PFI treatment, which illustrates that the PFI refining is a relatively mild mechanical treatment, as the results of XRD in Online Resource (Figures S1 and S2) show. In general, the CI-XI and the CI-XA of softwood fibers showed a reduction of 4.66% and 15.47%, respectively, and those of hardwood fibers decreased by 2.65% and 19.4%, respectively, as can be seen in Figure 4 and Table 1. The value of the CI-XI was remarkably higher than the CI-XA, which might be caused by the over-fitting of amorphous contribution in the analysis of CI-XA. However, the CI-XI and the CI-XA were correlated significantly for both softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, with a correlation coefficient of 0.919 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.925 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively, which is consistent with the report of Ahvenainen et al. 解析修复95块 · 要点 2/2；边界 2/2

文献结果显示，针叶木纤维湿纸幅强度的增幅比阔叶木纤维更显著，这与问题中的前提相反。 [3]
作者解释该差异的原因是纤维长度对湿纸幅强度起关键作用。 [3]
拉伸强度的提高主要归因于PFI打浆过程中不断增加的细纤维化和细小纤维。 [3]
PFI打浆使打浆度和WRV显著上升，原因是更高程度的细纤维化产生新表面和更多孔隙，润胀增加使纤维横向更柔顺，从而改善纤维网络的纤维间结合强度。 [6]
阔叶木的宏观细纤维化指数和纤维长度相对针叶木没有显著变化，可能是因为对阔叶木施加的打浆压力较低。 [6]

Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.",

These eﬀects\nof the PFI reﬁning on cellulosic ﬁbers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the ﬂexibility, and the\ninter-ﬁber bonding capacity of ﬁbers. It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and\nproperties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during reﬁning [7,8].\n\nThere are some diﬀerent conclusions regarding to the eﬀects of PFI reﬁning on crystallinity of\ncellulose, not like that of ball milling, which eﬀectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment\nprogresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI reﬁning\nfor corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased\nPolymers 2020, 12, 2912; doi:10.3390/polym12122912 www.mdpi.com/journal/polymers",
      "Polymers 2020, 12, 2912 10 of 14\nthe formation of O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI\n(as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the ﬂexibility of cellulosic ﬁbers, due to the higher mobility\nof molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of ﬁbers (as seen in Section 3.1).\nAs to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood ﬁber, the content had a growth\nof 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of reﬁning from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight\ndecrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of reﬁning.\nOverall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood ﬁbers, which ﬁrst increased and then had a\ndecrease, followed by a growth. During the whole reﬁning, the amount of O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds for\nsoftwood ﬁbers and hardwood ﬁbers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%,\nrespectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only\nless breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the\namorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important\nrole in the cellulose stiﬀness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose\nstiﬀness [33,34].\n\nIn the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood ﬁber, the trend of content\ncan be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of reﬁning\nfrom 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26%\nin the last reﬁning stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood ﬁber, it increased\nﬁrstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both ﬁbers, the content of\nO(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of reﬁning from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to\nthe fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than\nO(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.\nAs to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend\nin general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the\nbreakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and\nhigher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose\nmore accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber,\nthe number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions\nincreasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to\n12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups,\nwhich makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H···O(6) or O(6)H···O(3′)H-bonds. PFI2-031 · PFI打浆把纤维素从I型变成II型以后，结晶度为什么还会下降？

参考答案与评分要点

前提不成立：论文指出两种纤维的纤维素晶型在PFI处理中没有变化（依据附件XRD图S1、S2），作者据此认为PFI打浆是较温和的机械处理。结晶度方面，0→16000转总体下降但过程有波动，例如针叶木CI-XI由73.23%到69.82%。

表格行检索＋关联补全 · 要点 1/1；边界 2/2

所给证据不支持PFI打浆使纤维素由I型转变为II型：XRD结果表明两种纤维在PFI处理过程中纤维素晶型没有变化，PFI被视为相对温和的机械处理。 [3]
因此，“纤维素由I型变成II型后结晶度仍下降”这一前提与证据不符，不能据此把结晶度下降归因于晶型转变。 [3]
文献确实报道PFI精磨后结晶度指数下降：软木纤维的CI-XI和CI-XA分别降低4.66%和15.47%，硬木纤维分别降低2.65%和19.4%。 [3]
CI随精磨呈先降后升再降的波动，作者解释为机械作用先主要作用于结晶区，随后作用于无定形区并可能发生共结晶，之后又持续破坏结晶区。 [2]
引言指出PFI对结晶度的影响结论并不一致，有研究报道下降，也有研究报道先升后降或波动，并假设这些宏观结构变化与结晶度和H键网络变化有关。 [1]
结论认为总体上晶粒尺寸、结晶度和各种H键含量变化不大，PFI是对超分子结构破坏相对较小的良好机械纤颤处理。 [4]

  "task_id": "PFI2-031",
  "answer": "所给证据不支持PFI打浆使纤维素由I型转变为II型：XRD结果表明两种纤维在PFI处理过程中纤维素晶型没有变化，PFI被视为相对温和的机械处理。 [3]\n因此，“纤维素由I型变成II型后结晶度仍下降”这一前提与证据不符，不能据此把结晶度下降归因于晶型转变。 [3]\n文献确实报道PFI精磨后结晶度指数下降：软木纤维的CI-XI和CI-XA分别降低4.66%和15.47%，硬木纤维分别降低2.65%和19.4%。 [3]\nCI随精磨呈先降后升再降的波动，作者解释为机械作用先主要作用于结晶区，随后作用于无定形区并可能发生共结晶，之后又持续破坏结晶区。 [2]\n引言指出PFI对结晶度的影响结论并不一致，有研究报道下降，也有研究报道先升后降或波动，并假设这些宏观结构变化与结晶度和H键网络变化有关。 [1]\n结论认为总体上晶粒尺寸、结晶度和各种H键含量变化不大，PFI是对超分子结构破坏相对较小的良好机械纤颤处理。 [4]",

      "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Thus, according to the crystallite sizes (as Table 1 shows) and the unit cell parameters of cellulose Iβ, there was most likely to be an average of two-fibrils with an arrangement of 234,432 packed side-by-side for both softwood fibers and hardwood fibers (as seen in Figure 5, drawn with mercury",

Results and Discussions > 3.2. Effect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe cellulose polymorph of these two fibers had no change during PFI treatment, which illustrates that the PFI refining is a relatively mild mechanical treatment, as the results of XRD in Online Resource (Figures S1 and S2) show. In general, the CI-XI and the CI-XA of softwood fibers showed a reduction of 4.66% and 15.47%, respectively, and those of hardwood fibers decreased by 2.65% and 19.4%, respectively, as can be seen in Figure 4 and Table 1. The value of the CI-XI was remarkably higher than the CI-XA, which might be caused by the over-fitting of amorphous contribution in the analysis of CI-XA. However, the CI-XI and the CI-XA were correlated significantly for both softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, with a correlation coefficient of 0.919 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.925 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively, which is consistent with the report of Ahvenainen et al. [25].",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions\n[原文]\nThe results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Throughout the refining of two pulp fibers, the sizes perpendicular to (110) plane were more volatile than the (1\\overline{1}0) plane and (200) plane, which is consistent with the report of Duchemin et al., as shown in Table 1a,b [29]. It could be interpreted to be that water molecules were easier to permeate through the spaces between the hydrophilic (110) planes in paracrystalline region (hydration), and then it made these planes suffer more mechanical actions, so there was more adhesion (cocrystallization) and cleavage of cellulose chains created for (110) plane during PFI refining.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Introduction\n[原文]\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the differences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H···O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds differed at various refining stages.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining\n[原文]\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.",

解析修复95块 · 要点 1/1；边界 2/2

XRD结果显示，这两种纤维在PFI处理过程中纤维素晶型没有发生变化，说明PFI精炼是一种相对温和的机械处理 [3]
由于未发生晶型转变，PFI精炼中结晶度下降应归因于机械作用对结晶区的破坏，而不是多晶型转变 [3] [2]
结晶度变化呈先降、后升、再降的波动：第一阶段结晶度下降表明机械处理主要作用于结晶区 [2]
随后结晶度回升，可能是PFI精炼的机械与热作用下，更大的力作用于无定形区，并在干燥时发生共结晶 [2]
其后的再次下降则可能是结晶区被持续破坏所致 [2]
总体而言，软木纤维CI-XI和CI-XA分别下降4.66%和15.47%，硬木纤维分别下降2.65%和19.4% [3]
水分子更易渗入准晶区中亲水的(110)晶面之间（水合作用），使这些晶面承受更多机械作用，从而在PFI精炼中产生更多黏合（共结晶）和纤维素链断裂 [5]
两种纤维垂直于(200)晶面的微晶尺寸在PFI精炼中呈上升趋势，这可解释为纤维素链的合并或相邻微纤的结晶学堆叠，即(200)晶面在干燥时取向一致 [5]
(200)晶面上升还可能是因为水分子难以渗入，该晶面受到的断裂作用较弱 [5]
PFI精炼的主要作用包括纤维壁的分层、松散与润胀（内部细纤维化），以及纤维表面的细纤维剥离（外部细纤维化）等 [1]
研究结论认为，PFI精炼是一种优良的纤维化机械处理，对超分子结构的破坏相对较小，微晶尺寸、结晶度和各种氢键含量总体上变化不大 [4]

  "answer": "XRD结果显示，这两种纤维在PFI处理过程中纤维素晶型没有发生变化，说明PFI精炼是一种相对温和的机械处理 [3]\n由于未发生晶型转变，PFI精炼中结晶度下降应归因于机械作用对结晶区的破坏，而不是多晶型转变 [3] [2]\n结晶度变化呈先降、后升、再降的波动：第一阶段结晶度下降表明机械处理主要作用于结晶区 [2]\n随后结晶度回升，可能是PFI精炼的机械与热作用下，更大的力作用于无定形区，并在干燥时发生共结晶 [2]\n其后的再次下降则可能是结晶区被持续破坏所致 [2]\n总体而言，软木纤维CI-XI和CI-XA分别下降4.66%和15.47%，硬木纤维分别下降2.65%和19.4% [3]\n水分子更易渗入准晶区中亲水的(110)晶面之间（水合作用），使这些晶面承受更多机械作用，从而在PFI精炼中产生更多黏合（共结晶）和纤维素链断裂 [5]\n两种纤维垂直于(200)晶面的微晶尺寸在PFI精炼中呈上升趋势，这可解释为纤维素链的合并或相邻微纤的结晶学堆叠，即(200)晶面在干燥时取向一致 [5]\n(200)晶面上升还可能是因为水分子难以渗入，该晶面受到的断裂作用较弱 [5]\nPFI精炼的主要作用包括纤维壁的分层、松散与润胀（内部细纤维化），以及纤维表面的细纤维剥离（外部细纤维化）等 [1]\n研究结论认为，PFI精炼是一种优良的纤维化机械处理，对超分子结构的破坏相对较小，微晶尺寸、结晶度和各种氢键含量总体上变化不大 [4]",

      "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.",

Effect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nIt is known that both the (1\\overline{1}0) and the (110) lattice plane are hydrophilic, and the (200)lattice plane is hydrophobic in cellulose Iβ (as Figure 5 shows). In addition, it is noticeable that the (110) planes possess the highest theoretical roughness and accessibility to the hydrophilic groups in cellulose Iβ [28]. Throughout the refining of two pulp fibers, the sizes perpendicular to (110) plane were more volatile than the (1\\overline{1}0) plane and (200) plane, which is consistent with the report of Duchemin et al., as shown in Table 1a,b [29]. It could be interpreted to be that water molecules were easier to permeate through the spaces between the hydrophilic (110) planes in paracrystalline region (hydration), and then it made these planes suffer more mechanical actions, so there was more adhesion (cocrystallization) and cleavage of cellulose chains created for (110) plane during PFI refining.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Effect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nHowever, the crystallite size that was perpendicular to (200) lattice plane of two fibers had an upward trend during PFI refining. It could be explained in terms of coalescence of chains or some crystallographic stacking of adjacent microfibrils, where the (200) planes were aligned upon drying [30]. Additionally, it was probably due to the weaker cleavage effect on (200) lattice planes that was hard for water molecules to penetrate.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.",

Effect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4.
